sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 9.1% from $23.7 billion in FY2016 to $51.8 billion in FY2025 on the table's basis, which differs from as-reported totals in every year [F168][F1][F10][R1].
The path was cyclical: revenue fell 58.0% in FY2020 [D161] and rose 153.2% in FY2021 [D200].
Revenue rose 76.5% in FY2022 [D238] on higher realized prices and volumes, mainly from the Shell Permian acquisition [P59].
Net income then fell from $18.7 billion in FY2022 [F17] to $7.99 billion in FY2025 [F20], a three-year CAGR of -24.7% [D845].
Lower 48 contributed 8.0pp [D713] of FY2025 revenue growth of 4.9% [D342] and makes up 70.2% of revenue [D711].
Production rose 332 MBOED, mainly from new wells in the Delaware, Eagle Ford, Bakken and Midland basins and the Marathon Oil acquisition [P16][D342].
Lower realized crude prices offset much of the volume gain in revenue [P28][D342].
Cost of revenue rose 11.6% [D352] on revenue growth of 4.9% [D342], and net income fell 13.6% [D343].
Basic EPS fell 18.7% [D344], faster than net income [D343], as diluted shares rose 6.1% [D356].
Net margin of 15.4% in FY2025 [F30] sits below the window median of 17.9% [D831] and the FY2022 high of 30.6% [D830].
The table has no operating income line, so operating and gross margin cannot be measured here.
The effective tax rate rose to 36.9% [D332] from 32.4% [D298], so tax of $4.67 billion [X101] took more of pre-tax income of $12.7 billion [X91].
Purchased commodities and production costs both rose on the Marathon Oil acquisition [P24][P25], lifting cost of revenue 11.6% [D352].
Net margin rose 43.1pp in FY2021 [D208], above the 41.8pp fall in FY2020 [D170], and the filings cited do not explain it.
Operating cash flow of $19.8 billion [F59] was 2.48x net income [D333], up from 2.18x in FY2024 [D299].
Cash flow fell 1.6% [D346] on lower commodity prices, mostly offset by Marathon Oil operations [P6].
Capital expenditure is carried only through FY2022 [F66], when it was 12.9% of revenue [D222] and 1.35x D&A [D228], so FY2025 free cash flow is not measured.
Operating cash flow rose 66.6% in FY2022 [D242] on higher realized prices and Shell Permian volumes [P52].
Net cash was $7.11 billion at FY2025 [D337], up from $6.13 billion in FY2024 [D303].
The table carries no noncurrent debt after FY2020 [F157], so FY2021 to FY2025 net cash excludes it and uses only the current portion of debt [X199][X203].
On that basis, net cash of 12.1% of revenue [D338] ranks at the 100th percentile of six energy peers [D850], against a peer median of -7.7% [D851].
Buybacks of $5.02 billion [X141] and dividends of $4.00 billion [X151] totalled $9.01 billion [D339], together 46 percent of operating cash flow [P31].
Revenue basis (high severity, all ten years) [R1]: FY2025 is $51.8 billion in the table [F10] and $58.9 billion as first reported [X10].
Net income has fallen three years running, down 15.6% in FY2024 [D309] and 13.6% in FY2025 [D343], which the filings tie to lower commodity prices [P34][P20].
Diluted shares rose 6.1% in FY2025 [D356] to 1.25 billion [X131], and the filings cited do not explain the increase.
The FY2023 revenue fall of 20.5% [D274] is dropped as a single-year commodity move [P47]; the SG&A recast and segment overlap [R3][R4] are not used.
Net margin: a reading below 15.4% [F30] would extend the decline, while holding above the 17.9% window median [D831] would signal recovery in the FY2026 10-K.
Operating cash flow: a fall below $19.8 billion [F59] would extend the decline, measured against a stated return framework of greater than 30 percent of cash flow [P31].
Dispositions: $3.2 billion delivered against a $5 billion target by year-end 2026 [P32]; diluted shares below 1.25 billion [X131] would show buybacks outrunning dilution.
